## Objective
- Build a complete, playable retro 3D FPS shooter set in a dark maze, with guns, enemies, ammo pickups, and dynamic audio.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (≤1280px wide) and read only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained browser game using Canvas raycasting and procedural visuals/audio, without external game libraries.
- Game is titled “Night Shift — Sector 09”; includes desktop and touch controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game interface, HUD, title/pause/end screens, responsive styling, and touch controls.
- Implemented maze generation, raycast rendering, weapons, enemies, pickups, minimap, combat, and Web Audio effects.
- `node --check game.js` completed without output, indicating no syntax errors.

### Active
- Browser testing and visual verification have not been completed.

### Blocked
- An `edit` call failed with `ECONNRESET`; subsequent edits succeeded. No known remaining blocker.

## Next Move
1. Open `http://localhost:3002` with `playwright-cli` and inspect the game in-browser.
2. Start the game, check console errors and basic gameplay, then capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.
3. Fix any issues found and summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI structure and screens.
- `style.css`: Visual design, HUD, responsive and touch layouts.
- `game.js`: Game logic, rendering, controls, combat, and audio.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A Python HTTP server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- The last attempted browser command was `playwright-cli --help`; no browser verification or screenshot has been performed yet.
